title: HCR of Patched/Recorded Cerebellar Molecular Layer Interneurons
author: Carly Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bck7iuzn
materials: Pre-warm the 30% probe hybridization buffer to 37°C
Pre-warm the 30% probe wash buffer to 37°C

Using the cut pipette tip transfer method, gently transfer the accute slice either face up to to a glass micro-slide or randomly onto a glass 24x50mm no.1 coverslip. Remove the excess 2x SSC with a 200ul pipette and place a few drops of ProLong glass antifade mountant (invitrogen P36981) on the slice before it dries out at all. Either coverslip the slide or create a coverslip sandwich making sure to not incorporate bubbles into the mount. This will be stable if stored in the dark for a number of days.

steps.title: Patch‑fill neurons with Alexa‑594
steps.instruction: Fill recorded cerebellar molecular‑layer interneurons with 100 µM Alexa‑594 via the patch pipette before electrophysiological recording.

steps.title: Acquire two‑photon morphology images
steps.instruction: Using a custom two‑photon laser‑scanning microscope (40×, 0.8 NA Olympus objective; pulsed laser Chameleon or MIRA 900, Coherent) excite Alexa‑594 at 800 nm, acquire Z‑stacks and L‑DIC images of each cell, record slice location, and process images in ImageJ.

steps.title: Fix slices in PFA
steps.instruction: Transfer recorded slices (200–300 µm thick) to a well‑plate, submerge in 2–4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) prepared in PBS (pH 7.4), and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash slices in PBS
steps.instruction: Wash fixed slices three times with PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Store slices in ethanol
steps.instruction: Place slices in 70 % ethanol prepared with RNase‑free water and keep at 4 °C; perform HCR within 3–5 days.

steps.title: Detach slices from cover slips
steps.instruction: If slices are still attached to a circular cover slip or the bottom of the well, gently nudge them off with a metal spatula.

steps.title: Prepare 8 % SDS solution
steps.instruction: Make approximately 30 mL of 8 % SDS in 1× PBS. If a white precipitate forms, vortex until the solution becomes clear.

steps.title: Transfer slices to SDS and incubate
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette whose tip has been cut diagonally to a 3.5–4.0 mm opening, gently move slices from ethanol into the SDS solution (never press on the slice; swirl the dish or pipette up/down nearby so the slice floats, lift it within the enlarged tip, and expel it gently into the new well). Cover the plate with tin foil or a box, keep in the dark, and incubate at room temperature for 2 hours with agitation.

steps.title: Prepare 2× SSC solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL of 2× SSC in RNase‑free water.

steps.title: Quick SSC washes to remove SDS
steps.instruction: Aspirate the SDS solution carefully (avoid roughing the slice) and add 2× SSC. Repeat this aspiration and refill three times to quickly rinse out SDS.

steps.title: One‑hour SSC washes with agitation
steps.instruction: After the third quick wash, aspirate the SSC, add fresh 2× SSC, cover the plate with foil, and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature with agitation. Repeat this wash two more times (total three 1‑hour washes).

steps.title: Add hybridization buffer to new plate
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL of warmed hybridization buffer to each of four wells in a fresh well plate.

steps.title: Transfer slices to hybridization plate
steps.instruction: Using the cut‑open pipette tip, gently move the slices from the SSC‑filled plate into the wells containing hybridization buffer and relabel the plate.

steps.title: Incubate briefly at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the slices for 5 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare probe mix with RNase inhibitor
steps.instruction: For each sample, prepare 700 µL of pre‑warmed hybridization buffer containing RNase inhibitor at 1:100. Add 1.4 µL of the specific probe to the 700 µL buffer. Record which probe matches which hairpin set for later amplification.

steps.title: Replace buffer with probe mix
steps.instruction: Aspirate the initial 700 µL of hybridization buffer from each well and add the 700 µL probe mix prepared above.

steps.title: Humidify plate and seal
steps.instruction: Fill four empty wells of the plate halfway with water to create humidity, then tightly wrap the plate edges with parafilm to prevent drying.

steps.title: Overnight hybridization at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate overnight (≈16 h) at 37 °C.

steps.title: Probe wash series at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Using a box that fits over the plate for rapid exchanges, aspirate the probe mix and refill each well with warm probe‑wash buffer. Wash for 15 minutes at 37 °C, then repeat the aspirate‑refill‑wash cycle two more times (total three 15‑minute washes).

steps.title: Final SSC rinse at room temperature
steps.instruction: Aspirate the probe‑wash buffer and add 2× SSC to each well; incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Pre‑amplification buffer incubation
steps.instruction: Aspirate the SSC and add amplification buffer; incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare hairpin amplification cocktail
steps.instruction: During the 30‑minute pre‑amp incubation, prepare the amplification cocktail by adding 14 µL of each required hairpin to 700 µL of amplification buffer for each sample (snap‑cool protocol). Ensure the hairpin set matches the previously used probe.

steps.title: Add amplification cocktail to slices
steps.instruction: Aspirate the pre‑amp buffer and add 700 µL of the hairpin amplification cocktail to each well.

steps.title: Amplify signal and overnight storage
steps.instruction: Incubate the slices in the amplification cocktail for a minimum of 4 hours at room temperature, then place the plate at 4 °C and store overnight.

steps.title: Post‑amplification SSC washes
steps.instruction: Aspirate the amplification cocktail and fill wells with fresh 2× SSC. Wash for 10 minutes at room temperature, then repeat this wash two more times (total three 10‑minute washes). Samples remain stable in 2× SSC for a few days, but imaging should be performed as soon as possible.

steps.title: Mount slices for confocal imaging
steps.instruction: If the slice orientation is known (top side identified during recording), mount the slice on a glass slide; if orientation is unknown, mount the slice between two coverslips. Keep mounted samples protected from light.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Image the samples on an Andor CSU‑X spinning‑disk confocal system attached to a Nikon Eclipse Ti microscope equipped with an Andor iKon‑M camera. Use an oil‑immersion 60× objective, collect the Alexa‑594 channel together with the HCR probe/hairpin channels, and project a 10–20 µm thick z‑series for clear association of the patched cell with gene‑expression signals.
